accuracy.evidence: Basic needs (food, water, oxygen, shelter, suitable conditions) checked against the Year 2 NC statement on habitats meeting basic needs; clownfish on warm shallow reefs eating zooplankton and algae, protected by a mucus coat from host anemone stings (NOAA Ocean Service, Smithsonian Ocean); fish take dissolved oxygen through gills while dolphins are mammals with lungs breathing via a blowhole (NOAA Fisheries, Natural History Museum); green sea turtles graze seagrass; emperor penguins in Antarctic waters catching fish; anglerfish in the deep sea with a bioluminescent lure; sea stars on rocky shores.

misconceptions.evidence: Targets documented early-years ideas: sea animals only need sea water (food prediction, the 'just sea water' card, m4, tag drink); fish need no oxygen or gulp air at the surface (air prediction, 'Fish: swim up for air' button, p5, tag gills); dolphins breathe with gills (m1, tag blow); all sea water is the same so any animal can live anywhere (place prediction, wrong-zone feedback, m2, tag place); sea animals need different things from land animals (same-needs prediction, m6, tag land).

lab_distinct.evidence: flagseaneed is built around the sea meeting needs: food cards dragged onto a clownfish, seal and green turtle; a clownfish dragged into a drawn anemone and a crab under a rock while a big fish waits; tapping a fish's gills for bubbles and dragging a dolphin up to the surface to refill a breath bar; four animals placed into reef, polar, deep and shore zones; and land versus sea cards sorted into food, a safe place and air. flagneeds is needs versus wants, flaghome land homes, flagocean and flagoce5 what and where oceans are.

lab_teaches.evidence: Each idea is discovered first: the sea-water card is rejected because it is not food; dropping the clownfish in open water sends it back with the big-fish warning; the dolphin's breath bar only fills at the surface while the fish breathes where it is; a clownfish dropped in the icy sea is told the zone is freezing cold and what it needs instead; the counts in the three sort boxes end at 2/2 each, one land and one sea card per need. The step text then names shelter, oxygen and suitable conditions.

predictions.evidence: Five predictions with a tempting wrong option: 'no, they just drink sea water', 'out in the open water' (an anemone stings, so it looks unsafe), 'it swims up to breathe air', 'yes, all sea water is the same', and 'no, sea animals need different things'. Each is overturned by the task that follows, and the reveal line names the right answer.

challenge_feedback.evidence: Seven rotating questions (all needs, why the anemone, fish oxygen, dolphin breathing, clownfish in icy water, which need hiding meets, seal and fox alike). Wrong options carry tags drink, hide, gills, blow, place, sort and land, each with its own message naming the slip, e.g. 'A dolphin has no gills. It swims up and breathes air through its blowhole.'

readability.evidence: Kid text FK grade 2.3 and adult 8.1 (family targets 5.0 and 10.0); sentences are short and concrete (A seal eats fish. A crab tucks itself under a rock). Young-mode buttons are 56 px tall with larger text. Curriculum words shelter, oxygen, gills, habitat and suited are introduced with a plain meaning.

no_filler.evidence: Kid paragraphs: food, shelter, oxygen, the right part of the ocean. Adult: NC link and key words, facts with the mechanism (mucus coat, dissolved oxygen, lungs and blowhole), five named mistakes, then exactly what the lab does. No filler pattern matched and the 12% overlap gate passed against 554 What Living Things Need and 390 Where Animals Live.

mobile.evidence: Checked 360 px Android dark and iPhone 13 light screenshots of every step after Show me: food cards in a 2 × 2 grid, the rock and anemone sit above the feedback strip after moving them up, the breath bar was raised from 92% to 79% of the canvas height so the strip no longer hides it, zone cards end above the strip and show the ✓ animal names, and the feedback strip grows to four lines so the last sentence is no longer clipped.

accessibility.evidence: Every drag has a button twin: 'Give <food>' (labelled with the current animal), 'Clownfish into the anemone' / 'Leave clownfish in open water' / 'Crab under the rock' / 'Crab into the anemone', 'Fish: use its gills' / 'Fish: swim up for air' / 'Dolphin: swim up', one button per ocean zone and one per need. The canvas aria-label and live region carry each message. walk.cjs passed axe WCAG 2.1 AA in both themes on desktop and iPhone 13 with no console errors.

sources: National Curriculum in England: science programmes of study, Year 2 Living things and their habitats; Year 1 Animals, including humans (DfE, 2013)
NOAA Ocean Service: How do clownfish and anemones help each other? (mucus coat, protection from predators, warm reef habitat)
NOAA Fisheries: Green turtle (seagrass diet); Common bottlenose dolphin (mammal, lungs, blowhole)
Smithsonian Ocean: Fish (gills take dissolved oxygen from water); Deep sea anglerfish (bioluminescent lure)
British Antarctic Survey: Emperor penguin (Antarctic sea ice, diet of fish, krill and squid)
